llm.summary: The skill's instructions broadly match its stated purpose (lead discovery from public forums), but there are inconsistencies around required credentials and a changelog note that suggest you should verify how keys and environment variables are handled before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill is a lead-prospecting API wrapper and its declared requirements (an API key and an optional API base URL) are generally consistent with that purpose. However, the prose repeatedly states a 'zero-configuration free tier' that works out of the box with platform-provided keys, while the metadata (clawbot metadata in SKILL.md) lists SIMPLY_SEMANTICS_API_KEY as a required/primary environment variable. That mismatch is unexplained and incoherent: either the skill truly needs a user-supplied key or it uses platform keys — both claims appear in the package.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are narrowly scoped: extract targeting criteria from the user, validate input, then call the MCP-compatible POST endpoint with x-api-key header. They explicitly warn about the default 'mock' strategy. The instructions do not tell the agent to read unrelated files or credentials. One potential issue: the changelog mentions a 'dashboard deploy script dynamically gathers env vars from all service .env.production files' — that is not part of the runtime instructions but suggests the service/deployment may collect environment variables during deploy; this is worth clarifying with the publisher.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec or code files. Nothing is written to disk and there are no third-party packages being installed by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill metadata requires a single credential SIMPLY_SEMANTICS_API_KEY which is reasonable for an API-based SaaS. The concern is the apparent contradiction: documentation says free tier works with platform-provided keys and 'no configuration required', yet the skill marks the API key as required and primary. Additionally, the optional SEMANTIC_PROSPECT_API_BASE lets callers override the endpoint — which is useful but could be misused to redirect data to an arbitrary endpoint if you set it. The changelog line about gathering .env.production env vars is a further red flag that should be explained by the publisher (why and how env vars are scanned/gathered).

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent system privileges, does not set always:true, and contains no install or configuration that writes to other skills or system-wide config. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but is not combined with other high-risk indicators here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or providing credentials, verify the following: (1) Clarify the API key expectation — confirm whether the skill actually works with platform-provided keys or requires you to set SIMPLY_SEMANTICS_API_KEY; ask the publisher to resolve the contradiction. (2) Prefer creating a dedicated, limited-scope API key (if required) rather than reusing account-wide credentials. (3) Do not set SEMANTIC_PROSPECT_API_BASE to an untrusted endpoint — that would redirect all prospect payloads. (4) Ask the vendor to explain the changelog statement about 'gathering env vars from all service .env.production files' — confirm whether their dashboard or deploy scripts ever collect environment variables, and what they do with them. (5) Test with the default mock strategy first and review returned sample leads and privacy behavior. (6) Confirm data-retention, sharing, and privacy policy for collected lead/contact hints and ensure scraping public communities complies with each source's terms of service. If the publisher can't clearly explain the credential/collection behavior, treat the integration as higher risk and avoid providing sensitive environment variables.
